topic: The Pi-Collision Paradox: Why Bouncing Blocks Calculate Digits of Pi
target_audience: University students (Physics/Computer Science focus) or curious high school students

sections.title: The Hook: An Unexpected Connection
lecture_lines: Two blocks bounce between a wall and each other.
The number of collisions matches digits of Pi.
This happens for mass ratios of 100 to the n.
animations: Animate rectangles bouncing against each other and a wall.
Overlay collision count, incrementing digits of Pi: 3, 1, 4.

sections.title: Phase Space and Momentum Conservation
lecture_lines: We model the system using velocity phase space.
Energy conservation defines an ellipse in this space.
Collisions appear as instantaneous reflections off the ellipse boundary.
animations: Draw v1-v2 plane with axis labels #FFFFFF.
Animate an ellipse representing energy conservation in #2ECC71.
Animate the collision point as it moves across boundary.

sections.title: The Geometric Mapping
lecture_lines: We map velocity space into a circular geometry.
Elastic collisions become billiard ball reflections in a circle.
The total arc length equals the digits of Pi.
animations: Transform velocity plane to a circle, #F1C40F.
Show billiard trajectory with reflections at #FFFFFF.
Highlight total arc length segment, color #E67E22.
Slow motion reflection showing constant angle.

sections.title: Synthesis and The 'Digits of Pi' Reveal
lecture_lines: Mass ratio 1 gives 3 collisions, Pi starts 3.
animations: Transition to Pi: 3.1415... appearing on screen.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Beauty of Abstraction
lecture_lines: Physics and math are deeply, unexpectedly linked.
Discrete events can manifest fundamental mathematical constants.
The Pi-collision paradox reveals beauty in abstraction.
animations: Fade in abstract geometric patterns, color #34495E.
Display the equation for Pi through collisions.
Show final aesthetic graphic of Pi and collisions.
